simpleDefinition: A Portfolio Management Service is when you give a money manager (with a SEBI licence) at least ₹50 lakh and they buy and sell stocks for you in your own demat account. It's a more concentrated, more hands-on version of a mutual fund.
proDefinition: Portfolio Management Service. SEBI-registered discretionary or non-discretionary mandate where the manager invests directly in securities held in the client's individual demat. Minimum ticket ₹50L (FY24 onwards). Fees can be fixed, performance-linked, or hybrid.
whyItMatters: This is the entry tier into India's professional active management market for HNIs.

simpleDefinition: An Alternative Investment Fund pools money from a few wealthy investors to do things mutual funds can't — like investing in private companies, real estate, or hedge fund strategies. Minimum ticket is ₹1 crore.
proDefinition: Alternative Investment Fund. SEBI-registered pooled vehicle across three categories: I (early-stage / impact), II (PE, real estate, debt), III (hedge fund-style long-short / quant). Minimum investment ₹1Cr; closed-ended structures common.
whyItMatters: AIFs unlock asset classes — private equity, real estate, long-short — that public markets cannot replicate.

simpleDefinition: GIFT City is a special economic zone in Gujarat where Indian and international investors can park money in dollars (or other currencies) under tax-friendly, FEMA-light rules. It's India's onshore answer to Singapore or Dubai for finance.
proDefinition: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City. India's IFSC (International Financial Services Centre), regulated by IFSCA. Allows USD-denominated investing, AIFs, family offices, banking, insurance — with a distinct tax and FEMA regime versus the mainland.
whyItMatters: GIFT City lets NRIs and Indian residents access global products onshore without offshoring capital.

simpleDefinition: The minimum return your fund manager has to deliver before they're allowed to charge a performance fee. If the hurdle is 10% and your fund earned 9%, no performance fee is owed.
proDefinition: The minimum return threshold (often 8–10%) above which performance fees accrue. May be soft (catch-up applies) or hard (only the excess above hurdle is fee-bearing). Critical lever in PMS / AIF fee design.
whyItMatters: A higher hurdle aligns your interests with the manager's — they only get paid for genuine alpha.

simpleDefinition: Compound Annual Growth Rate is the smoothed annual return a fund would have needed to earn to grow your money from start to end. It hides the year-to-year ups and downs but makes comparisons easy.
proDefinition: Compound Annual Growth Rate. (Ending / Beginning)^(1/years) − 1. Standard metric for time-weighted performance disclosure but ignores volatility, drawdown, and order-of-returns risk.
whyItMatters: CAGR is the universal yardstick for comparing one fund's returns against another's over the same period.

simpleDefinition: Assets Under Management is the total value of money a fund manages on behalf of all its clients. Bigger isn't always better — large AUM can hurt performance in concentrated strategies.
proDefinition: Assets Under Management. Sum of all client capital deployed in a strategy. AUM trajectory and capacity discipline are key signals: aggressive AUM growth in a small-cap PMS often degrades alpha.
whyItMatters: Watch how AUM is growing — funds that close early to new investors often outperform those that scale endlessly.

simpleDefinition: Net Asset Value is the per-unit price of a fund. In a mutual fund, it's how you know what your investment is worth on a given day. PMS doesn't use NAV — it uses portfolio market value instead.
proDefinition: Net Asset Value. (Total assets − liabilities) / units outstanding. Computed daily for MF and Cat III AIFs. PMS reports portfolio market value on individual demats; AIF Cat I/II report periodic carrying value.
whyItMatters: NAV is your daily price tag — but only meaningful for vehicles that pool capital into units.

simpleDefinition: Long-Term Capital Gains tax is what you pay on profits from selling investments you've held for over a year. For equity-style PMS and AIFs, it's currently 12.5%.
proDefinition: Long-Term Capital Gains. Equity holding > 1 year taxed at 12.5% (post FY24 changes). Debt instruments held > 36 months historically taxed at slab post FY24. PMS pass-through retains the underlying tax character of each trade.
whyItMatters: PMS strategies churn portfolios — a high-turnover manager generates more STCG (taxed higher) than a long-hold one.

simpleDefinition: Short-Term Capital Gains tax is what you pay on profits from investments held under a year. For listed equity it's 20% — meaningfully higher than long-term tax. Frequent trading inside a PMS generates this.
proDefinition: Short-Term Capital Gains. Listed equity holding < 1 year taxed at 20% (post FY24). Debt and unlisted at slab. PMS turnover directly drives STCG drag — high-turnover momentum strategies meaningfully under-index post-tax.
whyItMatters: A 25% gross CAGR with high turnover can deliver less post-tax than an 18% CAGR with low turnover.

simpleDefinition: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the regulator that licenses and supervises every PMS, AIF, mutual fund, and stock broker in India. Always check that your manager has a valid SEBI registration number.
proDefinition: Securities and Exchange Board of India. Statutory regulator under the SEBI Act 1992. Issues separate registrations for PMS (INP*), AIF (IN/AIF*), MF, and intermediaries. Public registers and disclosure cycles are searchable on sebi.gov.in.
whyItMatters: No SEBI registration → no legal recourse. The first 30 seconds of due diligence is verifying the SEBI number.

simpleDefinition: A performance fee is what your manager takes only when the fund beats a pre-agreed hurdle. It's meant to align them with you — they only win when you do.
proDefinition: Performance fee (carry / incentive fee). Typically 15–20% of returns above hurdle. Can be charged on full return (catch-up) or only the excess. High-water mark provisions prevent re-earning fees on prior losses.
whyItMatters: A 1.5% mgmt + 15% perf above 10% hurdle is materially different from a 2.5% flat — model it before you sign.

simpleDefinition: A flat annual fee charged on your invested amount, regardless of performance. If you have ₹1Cr in a 2% management fee fund, you pay ₹2L/year whether the fund made 30% or lost 10%.
proDefinition: Management fee. Annual ad valorem charge on AUM (1.5–2.5% typical for PMS). Independent of performance. Combined with brokerage, custody, audit, and GST, true cost-to-investor often runs 50–80 bps above headline.
whyItMatters: Management fees compound — over 10 years they eat far more than most investors realise.

simpleDefinition: The biggest peak-to-trough fall in a fund's value. If your fund went from ₹1.5Cr to ₹1.05Cr before recovering, that 30% fall is its max drawdown. It's the real test of whether you can stay invested.
proDefinition: Maximum drawdown. Largest peak-to-trough decline over a measurement window. More predictive of behavioural risk than volatility — investors panic at drawdowns, not at standard deviation. Demand 5- and 7-year drawdown disclosure.
whyItMatters: Most investors quit at drawdown, not at volatility — knowing yours in advance is half the battle.

simpleDefinition: The Foreign Exchange Management Act sets the rules for moving money in and out of India. If you're an NRI, FEMA decides what you can repatriate, in what currency, and through which accounts.
proDefinition: Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999. Governs cross-border capital flows, NRO/NRE/FCNR account regimes, repatriation limits, and PIS approvals. GIFT City operates under a relaxed FEMA wrapper for IFSC-domiciled flows.
whyItMatters: For NRIs, FEMA — not tax — is often the binding constraint on which products you can actually use.
